item.title: Generating proteins with complex functions
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01330-9

A simple generative model learns protein sequence and structure together with functional context, enabling the design of proteins with specified molecular functions and multiple structural states.
item.dc:title: Generating proteins with complex functions

item.title: Exploring nonlinear body oscillations for natural quadruped gaits
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01320-x

Schmidt et al. demonstrate that nonlinear normal modes can be used to develop natural, multi-gait locomotion in a compliant quadruped robot, leveraging its inherent mechanics. The approach offers a design tool to shape embodied intelligence in robotics.

item.title: A long-context generative foundation model for versatile RNA design
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01321-w

Huang, Lv, Gao and colleagues investigate RNA scaling laws and introduce EVA, a long-context RNA foundation model for function prediction and diverse RNA design, supported by experimental validation.

item.title: Generating proteins with computationally predicted functions and multiple states via multimodal diffusion
item.content:encoded:
Nature Machine Intelligence, Published online: 27 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s42256-026-01329-2

Jing et al. present ProDiT, a multimodal diffusion model that generates diverse, functionally conditioned proteins, including multistate proteins, expanding capabilities beyond existing generative protein design methods.
